paragraphs: Friend, this chapter is heavy, and I won't pretend it isn't. The LORD tells Jeremiah to skip the wedding, the funeral meal and the feast, because He says He has removed His peace, His loving devotion and His compassion from this people (Jeremiah 16:5). Then He says why. The people followed other gods and stubbornly followed their own evil hearts instead of obeying Him (Jeremiah 16:11-12). Turning from the LORD is never small, and He tells them so plainly instead of leaving them to guess.

But hold on, because the LORD doesn't end in the dark. He says, "the days are coming," and He promises to return them to the land He gave their forefathers (Jeremiah 16:14-15). He sees all their ways, so nothing about their guilt is hidden from Him (Jeremiah 16:17). And that same God keeps His promise to bring His people home. Hard truth and real hope sit in the same chapter, and I think that's because He means both.

Then the nations speak, and this is my favorite part. They say they will come to the LORD from the ends of the earth, and that what their fathers handed down was "nothing but lies, worthless idols of no benefit at all" (Jeremiah 16:19). Anything we make to lean on, whether it's wood, money or our own plans, cannot hold us up. So here's the question for you, baker: what are you leaning on? Lean on the LORD, because He is the One who tells us, "then they will know that My name is the LORD" (Jeremiah 16:21).
